why.a: PDFs are hard to edit once downloaded. A Word file lets you tailor your resume for each role, and many employers accept or require .docx.

data.a: Only in this browser (localStorage). There is no server database and we never collect resume content. Use “Export JSON” to back up or move to another computer.

jobsite.q: Can I use it on job boards?
jobsite.a: Yes. Upload the .docx as an attachment, or copy and paste its content into application forms.

pages.q: Are page breaks the same as in the preview?
pages.a: Close, but Word decides the final page breaks. The dashed lines in the preview only mark A4 page positions.

wordMarks.q: Why is there a small square next to headings like Education in Word?
wordMarks.a: That’s Word’s “keep with next” marker. It only shows while formatting marks (¶) are visible, never prints, and won’t appear in a saved PDF. It just keeps each heading attached to the content below it.

pwaInstall.q: Can I install it on my phone or computer?
pwaInstall.a: Yes — this site is a PWA. In Chrome or Edge, click the install icon in the address bar or choose “Install app” from the menu. On iPhone or iPad, use Safari’s Share → “Add to Home Screen”. It opens in its own window like a regular app, and your resume data still stays on your device only.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.p1: Resumate Partner requires no sign-up and has no accounts or server-side database.
Privacy.p2: Everything you enter is stored only in this browser’s localStorage. The Word file is generated in your browser as well and is never uploaded to our servers.
Privacy.p3: Clearing your browser data or clicking “Clear data” deletes this content. We recommend backing up with “Export JSON”.
Privacy.p4: We use Vercel Analytics to count anonymous page views. It uses no cookies and never records resume content.

About.title: About
About.p1: Resumate Partner is a small, independent tool for building clean, ATS-friendly resumes and downloading them as editable Word files.
About.p2: We built it because most resume builders either lock your file behind a sign-up or only export a PDF you can’t edit. Here there are no accounts, no uploads, and no paywall.
About.p3: Everything runs in your browser, and the layout is designed to be readable by both recruiters and applicant tracking systems.

getting-started.title: Tutorial: build your first resume in 3 minutes
getting-started.desc: From a blank page to an exported Word file — a full walkthrough of Resumate Partner.

p: Click "Get started" on the homepage. On your first visit, you can load the sample resume to see a finished example, or start blank. No sign-up, no upload — everything stays in your browser.
The left column has seven sections: basics, education, experience, projects, skills, certifications & languages, and about me — with a live A4 preview on the right.
You don't have to fill everything. Click the eye icon next to a section to hide it — hidden sections won't appear in the exported Word file.
Drag sections in the "Section order & visibility" panel to control their order in the resume — put your strongest experience first.
The checkup flags common issues: missing required fields, invalid email format, experience entries without company or title, descriptions without numbers, and more. Work through the list one by one.
Click "Download .docx" — the output is a real Word document you can keep editing.

Want versions for different jobs? Use the resume switcher in the toolbar to add or duplicate resumes — everything stays on your device. To back up or move to another computer, use "Export JSON" and import it later.

vs-platforms.title: How is Resumate Partner different from Cake, Canva, and other platforms?
vs-platforms.desc: No signup, nothing uploaded, and an editable Word file — how Resumate Partner compares to mainstream resume platforms.

p: Resumate Partner often gets compared to Cake, Canva, or the resume builders inside job sites — but they're actually different things. It's closer to a "privacy-first Word resume generator": no account, no upload, and you get a .docx you can keep editing. Here's an honest breakdown to help you pick the right tool for your situation.

body.h: When Resumate Partner is the right pick
p: A good fit if: you'd rather not create an account, don't want your personal data on a third party's servers, need a Word file you can keep editing, or want an English resume from a Chinese-language UI for overseas applications.
Not a great fit if: you want flashy design templates, want your resume discoverable by recruiters on a platform, or want AI to write the content for you — platforms do those things better.
The two aren't mutually exclusive: build a clean Word resume here first, then upload it to 104 or Cake. Get your own file first — decide later whether to hand your data to a platform.

why-resumate.title: Why build yet another resume tool?
why-resumate.desc: The motivation and the decisions — why no signup, why Word instead of PDF, and why your data never leaves the browser.

p: There are already plenty of resume builders — so why make another one? Because two pain points kept showing up while job hunting: nearly every tool asks you to register first (so your name, phone number, and work history end up on someone else's server), and most only export PDF — meaning one typo fix means going back to the platform and re-exporting.
Resumate Partner is the answer to those two things: no signup, no upload, and a Word file you can keep editing. This post records the key decisions and what they cost.

body.h: Decision 1: your data never leaves the browser
p: All resume data lives in the browser's localStorage — the server never sees a single field. No account system, no database, and therefore no "data retained or leaked by the platform" problem.

The trade-off is explicit: data is bound to one browser, so switching devices means exporting a JSON backup by hand, and clearing browser data wipes it. For the "writing a resume" use case, we believe privacy is worth more than sync convenience.
Most tools export PDF because it's easy — render once and done. But resumes always need one last tweak before sending, and a Word file lets you keep editing after download.

Technically we emit native .docx structures: real paragraphs, real bullet numbering, tab stops, and heading styles — not a picture or a table pretending to be a resume. It edits naturally in Word and parses correctly in ATS systems.

Deliberately no template picker. Single column, clear heading hierarchy, machine-readable structure — a design that's safe for both ATS parsing and human skimming, and it saves you from half an hour of template indecision.
The cost: people who want flashy design will be disappointed. But if you're applying to roles screened by an ATS, a clean layout is the right answer anyway.

The site UI language and the resume's content language are separate settings — you can build an English resume from a Chinese interface. For anyone applying to multinational or overseas roles, that's essential: fill things out fast in your native language, output in the language the recruiter reads.
Each resume remembers its own language setting, so a Chinese and an English resume can coexist — one version per job opening.

Put together, these trade-offs mean Resumate Partner won't be the most feature-rich resume tool — but that was never the goal. The goal is: open it, fill it in, walk away with a Word file that's yours — without handing anything over along the way.

verify-privacy.title: Is your data really never uploaded? Three ways to check
verify-privacy.desc: Don't take our word for it — open DevTools or pull the network cable and confirm that your resume data never leaves the browser.

p: Every website claims to care about privacy, but "trust us" shouldn't be the answer. Resumate Partner is built so you can verify it yourself — here are three checks, the first two of which need no technical background at all.

After opening the site once, go offline — turn off Wi-Fi, or press F12 and tick Offline in the Network panel. Then keep using it: edit your resume, switch pages, reload, download the .docx, export JSON.

This is the strongest possible proof: if any step needed to send your data to a server, it would break the moment you disconnect. Everything keeps working, which means your data never needed to leave in the first place.
Press F12, open the Network panel, then type in the editor, switch resumes, and hit "Download .docx" — watch every request that goes out.

You'll see static assets (JavaScript, CSS) and anonymous analytics events, but open any of them and inspect the payload — none of them carry your name, phone number, or experience. If you're skeptical, compare them against your resume fields word by word.

body.h: Check 3: look at where the data lives
p: F12 → Application tab → Local Storage — your entire resume JSON sits right here, and this is the only place it exists. The "Export JSON" button reads exactly this data, so you can see its full contents with your own eyes.
On the server side there is no database, no account system, and no endpoint that accepts resume data — there's nowhere for it to be uploaded even if it wanted to.

body.h: In the interest of honesty: what does get sent
p: The site uses Vercel Analytics to collect anonymous statistics — for example which page was viewed, and whether a downloaded resume was in Chinese or English. These events contain no resume content whatsoever, but they do make network requests.
So the accurate claim is "your resume content is never uploaded", not "this site never touches the network". We'd rather state it precisely so you can check it for yourself.
Privacy shouldn't rest on "trust us" — it should rest on "you can check". That's also why the data is deliberately stored somewhere you can see and export.
